subject: Argonaut: throughput & latency incident — closure coordination and exec acceptance
messages:
From: Susan Nguyen <susan.nguyen@argonaut.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@argonaut.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime failures during peak window — immediate help needed

Hi Markus / Kim,

Quick heads-up: we saw a sustained spike in 5xx errors and token-level latencies across our inference routes between 08:40-09:10 PDT this morning. Throughput dropped by ~45% during the window and several end-to-end requests timed out (~120s). Our ops team (Tom Li included) tried restarting client-side connections and traffic shaping but saw no improvement.

This impacted our checkout recommendation flow and triggered retail customers to report slow responses. We need a technical RCA and a mitigation plan that we can present to our execs by Friday (09/03). Please escalate and advise immediate mitigation steps we can apply.

Attaching our internal incident logs (abbreviated).

Thanks,
Susan Nguyen
Sr. SRE, Argonaut Systems
[attachment: argonaut_incident_logs_0901.txt (text)]

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Susan Nguyen <susan.nguyen@argonaut.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime failures during peak window — immediate help needed

Susan — thanks for flagging and sorry for the disruption. We're escalating to Eng now.

Immediate actions (already in flight):
- Spun up additional warm pool nodes in us-west-2 and diverted new requests to isolated pool.
- Enabled circuit-breaker fallback to smaller model variant for requests > 1s.
- Routing and rate-limiter thresholds adjusted for Argonaut tenant only.

I'll coordinate the RCA and a clear corrective-action plan. Can you confirm the top 3 SLAs you want included in the executive readout (p95 latency, 5xx rate, throughput delta)?

I'll follow up with a runbook and proposed timeline by EOD.

—Markus
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Realtime failures during peak window — immediate help needed

Team — forwarding Argonaut incident. High business impact (checkout recommendations). Need: RCA draft + mitigations + canary/readout for execs by 09/03 10:00 PDT.

Initial hypotheses (from telemetry):
- Kernel selector regression in last deployment favored a heavy fp32 kernel for long sequences, increasing per-token compute.
- KV cache fragmentation resulting in more cache-loading work per request (seen on nodes s-west-*).
- Suboptimal batching thresholds during burst traffic, leading to head-of-line latency for small requests.

Please own items:
- Karthik: root-cause deep dive + kernel selector telemetry + suggested rollback/patch.
- Jonas: KV cache metrics + pre-warm strategy + measurables for improvement.
- Grace: Batching policy adjustments and perf testing plan (include target p95).
- Kim: Customer comms + exec-facing summary + MoM template.

I'll coordinate with the Argonaut SREs and set a shared drive for artifacts.

-- Markus

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argonaut incident — RCA findings and immediate mitigations

Team — summary of what we validated this morning (short):
1) Kernel selector regression: a config flag released 08/29 bumped prefer_fp32_affinity=true for a subset of models. Telemetry shows those requests had ~2.4x CPU cycles/token and increased GPU kernel time. Reverting that flag in the selector reduces per-token time by ~38% in our canary.
2) KV cache fragmentation: GC heuristics were tuned for memory density on 08/15; under burst traffic we observed more frequent cache misses for long-prefix sessions on w-3/w-4 nodes. A pre-warm + sticky routing strategy reduces cache miss rate by ~62%.
3) Batching thresholds: bursty request patterns from Argonaut's recommendation route hit a batch size floor that forced serialization. Increasing batch_desire_threshold and enabling continuous batching for small requests amortizes overhead and lowers p95.

Immediate mitigations deployed by 09/02 14:30 PDT:
- Rolled back prefer_fp32_affinity flag for Argonaut traffic (selector reverted).
- Applied pre-warm PKV script to the warm pool and enabled tenant-sticky routing for 30 minutes.
- Adjusted batching: batch_desire_threshold + reduced max_warm_batch_delay to 6ms for recommendation route.

Attached: argonaut_rca_20260902.pdf (full RCA), mitigation_playbook_v1.md, config-diff-20260902.patch

Next steps (ownership):
- Jonas: production verify across 8-hour peak window; collect p95/p99 and 5xx breakdown (deadline 09/03 09:00 PDT).
- Grace: run regression harness for the new batching policy (09/03 morning) and confirm model-quality is unchanged.
- Kim/Markus: executive brief deck + customer readout (09/03 11:00 PDT internal; 09/03 15:00 PDT Argonaut).

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
[attachment: argonaut_rca_20260902.pdf (pdf)]

From: Susan Nguyen <susan.nguyen@argonaut.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@argonaut.ai>, contracts@argonaut.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argonaut: throughput & latency incident — closure coordination and exec acceptance

Markus / team — thanks for the clear RCA and the rapid mitigations. We validated the window from 09/02 14:30 onward and see the following in our telemetry:
- p95 latency on recommendation route improved from 1.9s -> 420ms.
- 5xx rate dropped from 2.7% -> 0.2% during peak.
- Throughput restored to >95% of baseline.

Our execs have reviewed the RCA and are satisfied with the technical explanation and the mitigations. We do have two follow-ups before formal sign-off:
1) A short postmortem readout for Argonaut execs (15:00 PDT today) — can you share the 10-slide deck and a 10-minute script?
2) Credits: because this was a customer-impacting outage, our procurement team (cc'd contracts@argonaut.ai) is requesting a credits conversation tied to the SLA.

Assuming the readout goes well, we can accept the RCA and close the incident. Please send the deck and the link to the shared drive.

Cheers,
Susan
Sr. SRE, Argonaut Systems

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Susan Nguyen <susan.nguyen@argonaut.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argonaut: throughput & latency incident — closure coordination and exec acceptance

Thanks, Susan — glad to see metrics look healthy.

Deck and brief script are in the shared folder (link below) and we've scheduled the readout for 15:00 PDT. I'll lead the 10-minute script; Karthik will cover the technical RCA and Jonas will review the post-deploy verification.

Shared materials: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcd-example-Argonaut-RCA
Jira ticket for follow-ups: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ARG-1123

On credits: Kim, can you loop in Pricing/Finance and start a credits proposal? We'll treat that as a parallel commercial conversation and keep the technical closure independent for now.

—Markus
VP, Customer Reliability

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: contracts@argonaut.ai, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Susan Nguyen <susan.nguyen@argonaut.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argonaut credits conversation

Hi Contracts team — thanks for joining. I'll put together a credits proposal and send a one-page SOW addendum tonight for internal review. Proposed next steps:
- Draft credit proposal aligned to outage duration & SLA terms (Kimberly).
- Internal Pricing review (24 hours).
- Commercial call with Argonaut to finalize (by 09/07).

I'll keep the RCA and closure independent; marking this as a commercial follow-up.

Kim
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
